title: Adobe Lightroom mobile can now open closed eyes in photos with a simple tap

claims.claim: Adobe announced that the mobile version of Lightroom can now open closed eyes in photos using generative AI with just a single tap.

evidence.quote: Adobe announced yesterday that the mobile version of Lightroom, available for iOS, iPadOS, and Android, can now open closed eyes in photos using generative AI with just a single tap.

claims.claim: The Lightroom mobile app is available for iOS, iPadOS, and Android.

evidence.quote: Adobe announced yesterday that the mobile version of Lightroom, available for iOS, iPadOS, and Android, can now open closed eyes in photos using generative AI with just a single tap.
Adobe announced yesterday that the mobile version of Lightroom, available for iOS, iPadOS, and Android, can now open closed eyes in photos

claims.claim: The Open Eyes feature has been available in Adobe's Photoshop Elements for nearly a decade.

evidence.quote: Being able to easily save an otherwise great photo by opening a subject’s eyes has been a feature in Adobe’s Photoshop Elements for nearly a decade

claims.claim: Open Eyes in Lightroom mobile uses generative AI so the replacement eyes match the lighting and pose.

evidence.quote: Open Eyes in Lightroom mobile instead relies on generative AI so the replacement eyes match the lighting and pose

claims.claim: The app uses other images of the same person in the Lightroom library as reference to match color, size, and shape.

evidence.quote: and the app will use other images of the same person in your Lightroom library as reference so the open eyes will accurately match the color, size, and shape of their own.

claims.claim: Users of the free version of the Lightroom mobile app can try the Open Eyes feature twice before being prompted to subscribe.

evidence.quote: Those using the free version of the Lightroom mobile app can try the Open Eyes feature twice before they’re given a prompt to subscribe to an Adobe Creative Cloud plan
